definitions.explanation: A waste sorting category in Japan for items that cannot be incinerated, such as metals, ceramics, glass, and certain plastics. Collection days and accepted items vary by municipality.

examples.japanese: {燃|も}えないゴミ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{水曜日|すいようび}→水曜日：00672_suiyoubi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧。
examples.english: Non-burnable trash goes out on Wednesdays.

examples.japanese: ⟦フライパン→フライパン：01025_furaipan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{燃|も}えないゴミ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分類|ぶんるい}される→分類する：25224_bunruisuru⟧。
examples.english: A frying pan is classified as non-burnable trash.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}し⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{時|とき}、{燃|も}えないゴミ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{出|だ}し→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{分|わ}からなくて→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧⟦{困|こま}った→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: When I moved, I had trouble figuring out how to dispose of non-burnable trash.

notes:
An essential term for daily life in Japan. Japanese waste sorting (⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{分別|ぶんべつ}→分別：07706_bunbetsu⟧) is strict and varies by municipality. Residents must separate trash into categories and put each type out on the designated collection day.

MAIN TRASH CATEGORIES:
- ⟦{燃|も}えるゴミ→燃えるゴミ：17105_moerugomi⟧ / ⟦{可燃|かねん}→可燃：26077_kanen⟧⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧: burnable trash (food waste, paper, wood)
- {燃|も}えないゴミ / {不燃|ふねん}⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧: non-burnable trash (metal, glass, ceramics)
- ⟦{資源|しげん}→資源：03167_shigen⟧⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧: recyclable waste (bottles, cans, PET bottles, newspapers)
- ⟦{粗大|そだい}ゴミ→粗大ゴミ：08045_sodaigomi⟧: oversized/bulky trash (furniture, appliances)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {燃|も}えないゴミ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧: to put out non-burnable trash
- {燃|も}えないゴミ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧: non-burnable trash collection day
- {燃|も}えないゴミ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{袋|ふくろ}→袋：00837_fukuro⟧: non-burnable trash bag

ALTERNATE FORMS:
- {不燃|ふねん}⟦ゴミ→ゴミ：00840_gomi⟧: non-combustible waste — the more formal equivalent used on official signs and in municipal documents
